messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A job laid out across an entire bench. a small screw head strips at the last moment. You are tired of repeating the same approach. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "i leave the screw head visible and tap the bench with a knuckle, then slide it back a fraction. the stripped edge catches the new shape, so i keep the old approach intact. i mark the new spot with grease and leave the old screw visible beside the bench."}, {"id": "R014", "response": "i tap the screw once with my thumbnail, then stop. i lean the bench against the desk, tapping the last strip once more. the screw stays bent, so i move it closer to the bench. i write the last line on a scrap and put it back on the bench."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "i press the screw head down, then leave it for one minute. that is the only way i know it is working. i keep the bench open, not touching the head."}, {"id": "R016", "response": "the screw head catches. i tap the bench, then look at the last strip. “that,” i say, though i keep the screw head spinning. “it says the screw goes into the bench, but that means I need the whole thing.” i pull the bench aside, then put the screw head back on the bench."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "Stop. I press the head back. No—the screw is gone. I move the bench. No—the head is not. I put the bench back. Then I write the last piece. I keep the screw."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "i turn the screw once between finger and thumb. the head bites the cloth. i leave the bench and put the screw down beside the bench. i leave the clock face against the wall. it has been wrong for a while now."}, {"id": "R019", "response": "i put the screw head on the bench and wait for the last scrape. the screw stays on the bench, though i do not say so. i put the head on the bench and leave the screw beside it. the job stays open."}, {"id": "R020", "response": "i turn the bench with my hand and mark the screw head with chalk. i run my thumb along the bench, then leave the screw head seated and mark the same spot with chalk. then i test the screw with my other hand, but leave the bench still so i can pick up the mark."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "i tap the screw head. i leave the bench. i turn the screw once."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "i tap the bench twice with my foot, then lean against the head. “the screw stays,” i say, and tap the head once with my thumbnail. “i write the last line beside it, then tap the bench twice with my fingertip.” i lean back and tap the bench once more, but the screw keeps moving toward the edge."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "i put the bench back and mark the last time with my thumb. the screw head stays, so i leave the bench. i lean my hand back over the bench and write the time on my palm. Sorry. i leave the screw in the bench. i keep the bench open and write the time on my thumb."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "i press the screw head flat and leave the bench bare. i wait for the next movement to come. i keep the bench open for a minute and count the beats with my nail."}]
